story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain from code, at counter level. A door shuts on an empty stand where an apron hangs, and the phone rings while two tables wait. Then comes the same stand in the closed room, with chairs up and the door shut. A dark panel on the stand lights, writes Haniya and AI host beside the apron, and silences the ringing phone, its lamp steady under voice rings, as the lights go out. A guest's phone beside the code opens a menu, a dish is tapped and Pay turns to Paid. The mark reaches the printer, a ticket prints and the cook starts the wok. The owner's $9,650 is stamped as his own count. Coins fill a jar under a FOX 26 tag. The rule card and the blank folder box follow. The same guest's phone times out beside a quote, and the panel takes an order while the jar takes its two tags.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain from code, read from above and then at the stand. Footprints leave the stand as the door shuts, the phone rings and a guest waits beside a blank pad, with the server's apron still on the stand's hook. Then comes the same stand in the closed room, with chairs up and the door shut. The dark panel on the stand lights, writes Haniya and AI host beside the apron, and silences the phone that has rung since the walkout. Its lamp holds steady under voice rings from the panel while the room's lights go out. A guest scans, taps chow mein, talks to the phone and pays. The mark crosses into the printer, the ticket prints and the cook starts the wok. The owner's $9,650 is stamped OWNER COUNT beside an empty RECEIPTS clip. Coins fill the jar under FOX 26. The rule card and the blank folder box follow. An older customer's phone can't lock on the code beside one customer's quote, and the panel takes the next order before the jar ends under owner says and no record shown.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The question 'who takes the order?' gets its first visible answer at the same stand from 8.04 s. No new person comes, and a device named Haniya takes the station and then the call, even in the dark closed room (c1, c2, c5). The panel's order at 54.17 s closes the answer, and the tags keep the tip claim on the owner's word without inventing an outcome.
story_review.weakest_transition: s1 to s2 at 7.68 s. The apron and hook carry across the cut. The open room with guests becomes a closed room with chairs up and a panel that s1 never showed, and table-wait's phone sits at the stand's left end, where s2 has it right of the panel. The jump in time motivates the rearranged stand. Whether a mute viewer reads 'same station, later, a device installed' rather than a continuity slip is a pixel question for the combined fourth review.

notes: Code-proven observations that I do not classify as blocking, each with my reason. Fixing them is optional and does not reopen this review. (1) table-wait (s1, 4.83 to 7.68 s) draws the desk phone at stand x -170, scale .8. Its centre is 20 stand units past the stand top's 150 end. On screen the body spans about x -166 to 120, so only its right part shows at the frame edge, and that part sits over the stand top. host-phone:b (x 60) and s2 (PHONE_AT x 70) put the phone right of centre. Identity survives and the visible pixels show support, so I record this as a continuity and support risk, not a failure. Moving table-wait's phone onto the top at about x 60 would remove it. (2) The panel appears on the stand in s2 without having been in any s1 shot. The time skip into the closed room motivates this, and it is how the replacement shows the job passing to the panel without a performer. (3) In s10 the Haniya panel is the floor-pole PolePanel by the pass, while s2 mounts the panel head in a desk cradle on the host stand with its pole clipped away. The panel stays recognizable by its bezel, screen and lit name, and s9 to s10 isn't a declared same-subject cut, so I don't block on it. The combined fourth review should judge whether a viewer reads it as the same host.

Pixel-scope risks for the exact-film reviews, not code verdicts. (a) In host-panel:b the ring starts dying on the cut frame (10.89 to 11.29 s), so the stop has to read against the ringing seen in shot 1. (b) The lamp core is about 10 px and its glow about 29 px in native pixels in host-panel:b, so the answered state rests mostly on the ring marks stopping and the voice rings. (c) PanelHead clips HostPanel at bezel bottom +3, which cuts its .16-opacity halo along a straight line about 23 px past each bezel side. (d) The phone's handset overlaps the lower-right corner of the panel screen by about 68 by 15 stand units. (e) Haniya writes from 9.06 to 9.76 s, ahead of the word spoken at the clause end, and is held. (f) phone-timed-2's unresolved possible lateral jitter in s1 at 5.6 to 6.6 s still needs full-frame-rate checking. Nothing in the read source moves table-wait's FRAMES. (g) ClosedRoomFilm rewrites the other nine scenes 'in another shape', so their current pixels must be proven again at the combined fourth review.
